svg.aria-label: Stateless address autoconfiguration: link-local address, router solicitation, router advertisement with a prefix, and duplicate address detection

g.text: 1. makes fe80::… for itself, checks nobody has it
prefix 2001:db8:4c1:12::/64, and “use me as your router”
2001:db8:4c1:12: + an interface ID of its own choosing
from ::, “I don’t have an address yet”
…silence: nobody else has it. It’s mine.

ol.li: Every IPv6 interface gives itself a link-local address (fe80:: and an interface ID) the moment it comes up, and checks that nobody else is using it. It can already talk to everything on its own network.
Then it asks for routers, with a router solicitation to ff02::2, the group every router joins.

The router answers with a router advertisement: the network’s prefix, a flag saying “make your own addresses from this”, and how long to use it as the default router. Routers also send these every few minutes, unasked.
The laptop sticks an interface ID of its own onto the prefix. There’s no DHCP server keeping a list: this is stateless address autoconfiguration, SLAAC.

Before using it, it checks nobody else has it: “duplicate address detection”, a neighbour solicitation sent from the unspecified address ::. If nobody answers within a second, the address is its own, and it’s online.

figure.figcaption: How a computer gets an IPv6 address with no DHCP server at all.
